findings.title: Adjacent film/profile pairs repeat their middle rather than advancing the journey

locations.section: A film must also travel / What the national award recognises
Making a film for younger viewers

evidence: Bhukha describes western/coastal reception and separate promotion expense; Sabyasachi repeats both immediately afterwards.
Aadim Vichar award is recounted in Bhukha, Sabyasachi and the following Aadim film chapter.
Lavanya Preeti is immediately followed by Bir, whose first main section repeats its premise, alternative title and award.
findings.impact: Continuous readers repeatedly pause at already established milestones; distinctive teaching, family collaboration and children’s festival work receive less emphasis.
findings.bounded_correction: Keep full distribution detail in Bhukha and full award detail in the film chapters. Shorten corresponding profile recaps to one cited sentence/link; retain the son discussion and literacy/festival work. Do not delete award-year qualifications or rewrite these as new anecdotes.

findings.title: Uttam cross-link promises a collaboration the destination does not describe
findings.excerpt: The Sabyasachi Mohapatra profile follows that shared work from the filmmaker’s side.
findings.evidence: Destination discusses the director’s son, Bhukha distribution and Aadim Vichar credits; Uttam is not mentioned.
findings.impact: Reader follows a specific promise and receives a different account. This is a link-description mismatch, not evidence that the people never collaborated.
findings.bounded_correction: Change only link introduction to say it follows Sabyasachi’s other collaborations, or move this link to Further reading.

findings.title: The online part opener requires a much longer detour than the book opener
findings.evidence: Online overview has approximately5746 whitespace-separated tokens before notes and21H2 headings; it follows five Songs and Voices readings and repeats radio/song context already encountered. Book deliberately uses the brief restoration/1936 opening and places the wider survey in its appendix. Web Continue reading occurs only at narrative end.
findings.impact: A sequential web reader encounters a long reference survey before reaching Gour, while a book reader quickly proceeds to the lives.
findings.bounded_correction: Consider one early optional link after the overview opening to continue to Gour, labelled as a shorter reading path; preserve the full survey, headings, sources and standard bottom navigation. No extra article or mandatory reorder needed.

findings.title: Several brief profiles explain their examples repeatedly

locations.section: A classroom could become a stage

evidence: Bijay’s prop/building testimony is followed by a paragraph explaining what a prop and building ask of performers.
Uttam’s short memories are each followed by general reflection and/or a link paragraph.
Lipika’s second paragraph repeats the opening question about people beyond performance.
Manmohan closing repeats Jayaswami and camera-loan recollections already told.
findings.impact: Across consecutive profiles this produces a fact–explanation–invitation rhythm and reduces the force of the concrete testimony.
findings.bounded_correction: Cut only redundant interpretive sentences; retain one closing invitation per article and all named testimony/citations. Do not add invented scenes or pad short profiles.

findings.title: Collective learning chapter has not fully caught up with the new profiles

locations.section: Learning with the ear / Further reading

findings.evidence: Bijay Mishra’s named account sends readers to literature-and-screen, and Lipika’s named passage sends them to Sita Bibaha; neither now-existing dedicated profile is linked in this chapter’s body or Further reading. Lipika immediately precedes it in the main sequence.
findings.impact: Readers entering the collective chapter directly can miss the fuller lives already available; printed cross-references likewise miss an obvious destination.
findings.bounded_correction: Link the existing first mentions to Bijay and Lipika profiles; retain the literature and Sita links where they serve their distinct themes. No new content or profiles needed.

imagery.assessment: These four illustrations visibly support rehearsal, script exchange and childhood spectatorship. Captions call them illustrations and do not assert documentary likeness. Aparajita and Learning share a paper-discussion motif but show distinct compositions; not a duplicate-image defect. No new images recommended from this review.
imagery.metadata_assessment: Documentary captions name event/date where supplied; Parbati’s stamp and novel page add distinct historical/textual material. Full rights revalidation and all-image visual inspection were not repeated.

strengths: Women are active makers/mentors: Parbati, Aparajita, Bijaya, Nandita and Lipika; Sadhana informal story help remains distinct from screen credit.
Named camera, editing, sound and music contributors occur across film chapters; Lipika and Pramod provide sustained craft attention beyond a crew list.
Sambalpuri film identity, Odisha-origin Hindi work, award year versus release and festival selection versus prize remain explicitly distinguished.
Participant recollections and synopsis-derived plots are labelled; no scene reconstruction needed to improve prose.
contribution_coverage.limits: This is a selected connected series, not comprehensive role representation. A dedicated exhibitor/distributor or technician profile would require separate research; not a present factual defect or recommendation to expand this audit.
